_comment: Single source of truth for which model families can be picked as a routing target, and how. 'current_reference' is just an informational snapshot (for humans/Jev) - actual selection NEVER uses it, always the generic alias (see policy), which automatically points at the latest version. The concrete tier->target text is already given per provider by targets.json; this file is only the FAMILY-level policy (what's selectable at all).

claude.policy: Routing/agent config always uses the family's generic Claude Code alias (e.g. "sonnet", "opus", "fable"), never a pinned/dated model ID (e.g. "claude-opus-5-5" may not be used in config). The alias always points at the family's currently latest version. The Haiku family can never be selected as a routing target, not even via manual override (#tag).

effort_levels.source: this session's own live Claude Code environment: ~/.claude/settings.json's 'effortLevel' and per-family 'modelSettings' fields, plus the ReportFindings tool's 'level' enum. Not separately verified per family (sonnet/opus/fable) - assumed shared across all three.
effort_levels.note: JEV picks the effort level PER REQUEST from this list, not a fixed one - see router/core.py build_questions()'s 'effort' question. 'max' is the hard ceiling for Claude: there is no 'ultra' tier, unlike Codex's gpt-5.6-terra which uniquely has one. 'ultra' is excluded here at the CODE level too (core.py strips it even if a Jev answer somehow names it), not just by omitting it from the prompt - the same defense-in-depth principle as DESTRUCTIVE_RE backing up the Jev destructive-question.

codex.status: routing wired up (routes.json + targets.json) AND verified against real, current account data
codex.verified_against: ~/.codex/models_cache.json, fetched 2026-09-23T20:11:24Z, client 0.156.1 - see router/probe_models.py to refresh this

available_models.note: current generation, fast/cheap tier - used for 'fast' and 'main'
fast/cheap agentic-coding model, not currently mapped to a tier
previous generation, but the ONLY model with 'ultra' reasoning effort (adds automatic task delegation) - used for 'deep' until a gpt-6 tier above 'luna' ships
previous generation fast tier, superseded by gpt-6-luna, not currently mapped
legacy, only goes up to 'xhigh' effort (no 'max'), not currently mapped
automatic approval review model, not a general-purpose tier

effort_levels.note: Unlike Claude, Codex has NO blanket exclusion - JEV picks freely per request from the CHOSEN model's own 'levels' list above (each model's list differs; verify per slug, not per provider). 'ultra' is valid ONLY on gpt-5.6-terra - core.py passes it in build_questions()'s 'effort' criteria text as a caveat rather than filtering it in code, since which levels are valid depends on which model got picked in the same decision, and Codex (unlike Claude) has no hard per-provider ban to enforce.

codex.note: The UserPromptSubmit hook already runs before every Codex CLI prompt ONCE TRUSTED (see router/run_hook.py). Its additionalContext is advisory text only - the hook API cannot force a model switch mid-session. The actual model/effort is chosen at launch: `codex -m <slug> -c model_reasoning_effort=<level>`. There is no 'excluded family' here like Claude's Haiku ban - all 6 available models are usable, tiering is via reasoning effort on one model rather than swapping models, except for the deep tier (see targets.json).

hook_trust.status: NOT YET GRANTED as of 2026-09-23 - the hook does not fire automatically yet
hook_trust.finding: Verified live: a real `codex exec "..."` from a fresh directory produced NO logs/routing.jsonl entry (hook silently skipped). The identical prompt with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` DID fire the hook and log it (`hook: UserPromptSubmit` / `hook: UserPromptSubmit Completed` printed, log entry appeared). This is Codex's own security feature, not a bug in router/install_hooks.py: it never runs an unreviewed hook.
hook_trust.fix: Codex persists hook trust per-entry in ~/.codex/config.toml under a `[hooks.state...]` block, granted via a one-time interactive TUI prompt ('Hooks need review... Trust all and continue?') the first time a trusted-but-unapproved hook would fire in an INTERACTIVE (non-exec) `codex` session. Run plain `codex` (not `codex exec`) once, anywhere, and approve that prompt - it then persists for every future session, interactive or headless (`codex exec`), in any project, since it's stored at the user level. Until then, `codex exec` calls only get the router if launched with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`.

codex.agents_note: Custom agent roles: [agents.<name>] in ~/.codex/config.toml with description + config_file (a role TOML holding model / model_reasoning_effort / developer_instructions) - verified from the 0.156.1 binary's config schema (AgentRoleToml: description, config_file, nickname_candidates) and the multi_agent feature flag (stable, on). Generated by `python router/skills_hub.py agents` from targets.json -> codex.tiers.

antigravity.status: Logged in 2026-09-23 (keyring OAuth). Antigravity desktop app 2.17.0 (winget Google.Antigravity) + CLI `agy` 1.2.9 (%LOCALAPPDATA%gy ingy.exe) installed. Replaces Gemini CLI (Google ended its free individual tier).
antigravity.cli_home_note: Antigravity CLI reuses the ~/.gemini/ home directory tree (its own subfolder: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/), NOT a separate ~/.antigravity/ - confirmed by inspecting the install output. Global config (analogous to skills.json/hooks.json) lives at ~/.gemini/config/.

hook.config_path: project-local: .agents/hooks.json ; global: ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json (source: local doc ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/hooks.md, read directly off disk after install - not a web summary)
hook.format_difference: Unlike Claude/Codex, PreInvocation is NOT the same contract: (1) it fires before EVERY model call within a turn, not just once per user-submitted prompt (there's an 'invocationNum' sequence field) (2) its stdin has NO prompt text at all - only conversationId/workspacePaths/transcriptPath/artifactDirectoryPath/modelName/invocationNum/initialNumSteps (3) its stdout wants {"injectSteps": [{"ephemeralMessage": "..."}]}, not {"hookSpecificOutput": {"additionalContext": ...}}.
hook.trust: No trust gate observed: the hook was loaded ('loaded 1 named hooks') and executed on the first real run.
hook.transcript_format:
VERIFIED 2026-09-23 with a real `agy -p` run: transcriptPath points to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversationId>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl; the user's turn is a line with type=USER_INPUT, source=USER_EXPLICIT, content='<USER_REQUEST>
...
</USER_REQUEST>
<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>...'. It is already written when PreInvocation fires.
hook.windows_quoting: VERIFIED bug: Antigravity runs hook commands via `cmd /c`, and a quoted path with spaces ("E:/Coding Projects/...") breaks (python gets 'C:\Users\...\.gemini\config\\"E:\Coding'). Fix: hooks call the space-free shim ~/.jev-router/bin/run_hook.py (installed by router/install_hooks.py).

skills.mechanism: Cleaner than Claude/Codex: no directory junction needed. A skills.json manifest (project-local .agents/skills.json, or global ~/.gemini/config/skills.json) with an 'entries' array of {"path": "..."} can point directly at our shared skills/ folder - Antigravity scans each entry path one level deep. Source: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/json_configs.md.
skills.format_confirmed_cross_compatible: Yes - Antigravity's own skill docs state the SKILL.md format is the same open standard also used by Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI (matches what this repo already verified empirically for those two).
skills.path_rule: VERIFIED 2026-09-23 (agy 1.2.9): skills.json entry paths must be ABSOLUTE - '~/.skills' is rejected at runtime ('~/.skills must be an absolute path'), although the bundled docs claim '~/' is home-relative. Use a forward-slash absolute path without spaces: C:/Users/<user>/.skills.

effort_levels.source: `agy --help` (no auth needed): '--effort  Reasoning effort for the current CLI session (low|medium|high)'. Confirmed narrower than Claude (low..max) and Codex (low..ultra) - no xhigh/max/ultra tier exists for Antigravity.
effort_levels.note: Effort is baked into the model slug (…-low/-medium/-high); `agy --effort` sets it per CLI session.
